raw_statement: By 31 December 2031, grid reliability is treated as a purchased good rather than a public guarantee: annual unit sales of residential/commercial backup generation and storage (generators, home batteries, solar+storage attach) in the US and EU at least double versus 2025, corporate behind-the-meter and long-term firm-power contracting (LNG, nuclear PPAs, district heat) covers a materially larger share of large-enterprise load, and consumer search interest in grid-failure/outage preparedness stays structurally above its 2024–2025 baseline.
title: Reliability as a Purchased Good: Private Substitution for a Degrading Public Power Guarantee (2026–2031)

formalized.statement: By 31 December 2031, electricity reliability in the US and EU is behaviourally and commercially treated as a privately purchased good rather than an implicit public guarantee. Operationally: (1) combined annual unit sales of residential/commercial backup generation and storage (standby + portable generators, residential/C&I batteries, solar+storage attach) in the US and EU are at least 2.0x their 2025 level; (2) the share of large-enterprise (Fortune 500 / STOXX 600 industrial + hyperscaler) electricity load covered by behind-the-meter generation or long-term firm-power contracts (LNG-to-power, nuclear PPA, cogeneration, district heat) rises by at least 15 percentage points versus 2025; (3) the trailing-12-month consumer search index for grid-failure/outage-preparedness terms remains at or above 120% of the 2024–2025 mean in every quarter of 2031.
formalized.population: US and EU-27 households (roughly 130m + 195m dwellings), small/medium commercial premises, and large enterprises with >50 GWh/yr load including hyperscalers, data-centre operators, chemicals, steel, semiconductors and hospitals.
formalized.behavior: Voluntarily paying a private premium for electricity availability — buying, financing or leasing on-site generation/storage, or contracting bilaterally for firm dispatchable supply — instead of relying on the regulated utility's universal-service reliability promise.
formalized.observable_outcome: A structurally higher installed base of behind-the-meter capacity and firm bilateral contracts, visible in (a) Generac/Kohler/Briggs/Cummins/Caterpillar residential+C&I shipment data and EU BESS install statistics, (b) disclosed corporate PPA and BTM capacity in 10-K/CSRD filings and LevelTen/BNEF PPA trackers, (c) persistently elevated consumer outage-preparedness search and retail SKU velocity at Home Depot/Lowe's/Bauhaus.
formalized.measurable_metric: Composite index: (i) US+EU annual unit shipments of residential/commercial generators and behind-the-meter batteries (2025 = 100; threshold ≥200 in CY2031); (ii) percentage-point change in large-enterprise load under BTM or ≥5-year firm PPA (threshold ≥ +15pp vs 2025, from BNEF/LevelTen/company disclosure); (iii) Google Trends 12-month moving average of a fixed basket ('power outage', 'generator for home', 'grid failure', 'blackout preparedness', EU-language equivalents) indexed to 2024–2025 = 100 (threshold ≥120 in all four quarters of 2031). Thesis confirmed if (i) and at least one of (ii)/(iii) clear thresholds.

mechanism.human_motivation: Loss aversion around a service whose failure is catastrophic and non-substitutable (heat, refrigeration, medical devices, remote work, EV charging). Once the perceived probability of failure crosses a salience threshold — usually via one vivid personal or televised event — households and boards shift from optimisation to insurance, and reliability becomes a status/security consumption category rather than a utility line item.
mechanism.friction_removed: Historically self-generation required diesel logistics, permitting, noise, an electrician, and $10k+ of capital. That friction is collapsing: plug-in battery/inverter kits, integrated ATS panels, dealer-installed standby units financed on the mortgage or a lease, virtual-power-plant enrollments that monetise the asset, and — for corporates — turnkey BTM gas/fuel-cell/nuclear PPA packages sold by developers rather than built in-house. Interconnection queue delays (5–7 years) paradoxically remove friction from the BTM route by making the grid the slow option.
mechanism.enabling_technology: Cheap LFP cells and hybrid inverters; smart panels and automatic transfer switches; aeroderivative turbines and reciprocating gensets with fast delivery slots; fuel cells; SMR/nuclear PPA structures; grid-edge orchestration software (Emerald AI-type headroom products, VPP dispatch); cheap sensing and outage telemetry that makes unreliability legible in real time.
mechanism.economic_incentive: For enterprises: the cost of a data-centre or fab outage is measured in $M/hour, and AI load growth cannot wait for interconnection — BTM is a schedule purchase, not just a price purchase. For households: rising retail tariffs (grid-hardening capex, wildfire liability, transmission build) widen the spread between grid kWh and self-generated kWh, while VPP payments and capacity-market revenues create an income stream that partially funds the asset. Insurance pricing and spoilage/WFH-income loss add quantifiable avoided cost.
mechanism.trust_requirement: Inverse trust dynamic: adoption rises as trust in the public guarantee falls. Buyers must nonetheless trust the private substitute — installer quality, fuel availability, battery fire safety, warranty, and the counterparty's ability to deliver firm MW in 2029. Certification (UL 9540, CE, NFPA), utility interconnection approval, and lender/insurer acceptance are the trust rails.
mechanism.distribution_mechanism: Big-box retail and e-commerce (Home Depot, Lowe's, Amazon, Bauhaus, Leroy Merlin) for portables; dealer/installer networks and solar channels for standby and storage; homebuilders bundling into new construction; utilities themselves selling resilience-as-a-service; for enterprises, EPCs, IPPs and developers (Quanta, Bechtel, Talen, Constellation, NextEra, Bloom) plus direct OEM allocation deals with hyperscalers.
mechanism.network_effects: Weak direct, strong indirect. Installer density, fuel/service ecosystems, and VPP aggregation create local increasing returns; visible neighbourhood adoption (a humming generator next door during a blackout) is a powerful social-proof channel. Adverse loop: each defector reduces the revenue base funding grid reliability, raising tariffs for the remainder and accelerating further defection — a self-reinforcing utility death-spiral dynamic.
mechanism.switching_costs: High once installed: sunk capital, fixed gas/propane connection, roof and panel integration, financing tied to the property. This makes the installed base sticky and the thesis hard to reverse even if grid reliability improves — the behaviour ratchets.
mechanism.regulatory_constraints: Two-sided. Constraining: interconnection rules, net-metering rollbacks, air-permit limits on diesel/gas runtime hours (California BAAQMD, EU IED), noise ordinances, HOA rules, battery siting codes, EU capacity-market and self-consumption tax treatment. Enabling: FERC 2222 aggregation, state resilience rebates, IRA/CSRD-era incentives, EU energy-security rules post-2022, and explicit data-centre BTM carve-outs now being drafted in PJM/ERCOT and several EU member states.

analogues.name: Bottled water and home filtration substituting for municipal tap water (US/EU)
analogues.mechanism: A universal public utility's perceived quality/safety guarantee erodes; consumers pay a very large per-unit premium for a privately supplied substitute even where the public good remains objectively adequate.
analogues.lesson: Perceived reliability, not measured reliability, drives spend; once a public guarantee is psychologically privatised, consumption is sticky and price-insensitive for decades. Distribution through mass retail was the accelerant.

analogues.name: South Africa load-shedding → rooftop solar and battery boom
analogues.mechanism: Documented, repeated failure of the public electricity guarantee triggers mass private self-generation by households and firms within ~4 years.
analogues.lesson: The closest living laboratory: private BTM capacity rose from negligible to >5 GW in under five years and did NOT reverse when load-shedding paused. Adoption is event-triggered and ratchets; the trigger is repetition, not severity.

analogues.name: Diesel gensets as default infrastructure in Nigeria, India, Lebanon, Pakistan
analogues.mechanism: Chronic unreliability converts backup generation from an exception into a mandatory capital item for any commercial premises.
analogues.lesson: Where the grid fails persistently, private generation becomes a line item in every building budget and a permanent 5–10% tax on GDP. The end state of the thesis exists; the open question is how far the US/EU travel along it.

analogues.name: Japanese corporate self-generation and household solar+storage after Fukushima
analogues.mechanism: A single systemic shock destroys confidence in centralised supply; corporates and households buy on-site generation and storage as insurance against policy and physical failure.
analogues.lesson: One salient national event can permanently reset the willingness to pay for self-supply, but the size of the shift depends heavily on subsidy design (FIT) — policy converts fear into installed base.

analogues.name: Texas Winter Storm Uri → Generac standby generator demand surge
analogues.mechanism: Localised catastrophic outage raises perceived tail risk; residential standby generator penetration and order backlogs jump sharply.
analogues.lesson: Demand spikes are real but partially mean-revert: Generac's post-Uri backlog unwound by 2023. The thesis requires a *sequence* of events plus rising tariffs, not one shock, to produce a structural doubling.

analogues.name: Residential home-security systems and alarms (ADT, Ring) substituting for policing
analogues.mechanism: Private purchase of a security service that was nominally a universal public guarantee, driven by perceived risk and falling hardware cost.
analogues.lesson: Security categories grow slowly for decades, then inflect when hardware cost collapses and distribution becomes retail/DIY (Ring). Watch for the 'Ring moment' in plug-in home batteries.

analogues.name: Private security guards outnumbering police in the US/UK/Brazil
analogues.mechanism: Public provision spread thin → institutional buyers contract private substitutes for the same service at premises level.
analogues.lesson: Enterprise buyers move first and faster than households because the loss function is quantified; consumer adoption follows a decade later. Expect corporate firm-power contracting to lead the household generator cycle.

analogues.name: Enterprise UPS and on-site data-centre generation becoming mandatory
analogues.mechanism: As computing became mission-critical, N+1 power redundancy went from optional to a contractual/insurance requirement — reliability purchased, not assumed.
analogues.lesson: Once uptime enters SLAs and insurance underwriting, resilience capex becomes non-discretionary and survives downturns. The corporate leg of this thesis is the highest-confidence leg.

analogues.name: Corporate cogeneration build-out after the 1973/1979 oil shocks and PURPA
analogues.mechanism: Energy-price and supply insecurity plus regulatory enabling → industrials self-generate rather than buy from the utility.
analogues.lesson: Regulatory permission (PURPA) was the unlock, not technology. The analogous unlock here is BTM/interconnection carve-outs for data centres — watch the rulemaking, not the hardware.

analogues.name: Private health insurance / private GP usage alongside the NHS and European public systems
analogues.mechanism: Queues and degraded service quality in a universal public guarantee drive top-income deciles to buy a parallel private tier while still paying for the public one.
analogues.lesson: Partial, income-stratified defection is the most common outcome — not universal privatisation. The realistic 2031 state is a bifurcated market: affluent suburbs and large corporates self-provision, everyone else absorbs worse service and higher tariffs.

analogues.name: Gated communities and private residential infrastructure (roads, water, security) in the US and Latin America
analogues.mechanism: Households buy bundled privately-provisioned public goods when municipal provision is distrusted; capitalised into property value.
analogues.lesson: Once resilience capitalises into home prices and mortgage underwriting, adoption becomes builder-driven and automatic — the single biggest potential accelerant for residential storage attach rates.

analogues.name: Home air purification and HEPA adoption after wildfire smoke and COVID
analogues.mechanism: Environmental failure of an assumed-free public good (clean air) triggers rapid private hardware purchase.
analogues.lesson: Cheap, plug-in, no-install form factors adopt 5x faster than permitted/installed ones. Portable power stations will scale faster than whole-home standby, which matters for which manufacturers capture the volume.

analogues.name: Cellular/Starlink failover replacing single-ISP dependence for homes and SMBs
analogues.mechanism: Connectivity reclassified from utility to mission-critical; buyers pay for a second, independent path rather than trusting one provider.
analogues.lesson: Redundancy sells once the primary service becomes economically load-bearing (remote work). Power follows the same logic as WFH, EVs and home medical devices raise the cost of an outage hour.

analogues.name: Bottled LPG and wood-stove reversion during the 2022 European gas crisis
analogues.mechanism: Supply-security shock drives households toward self-owned, storable energy — but reverses once prices normalise.
analogues.lesson: Counter-case: heat-pump and wood-stove demand in Germany/Netherlands spiked in 2022 and fell hard by 2024 when prices and fear normalised. Fear-driven durable-goods demand mean-reverts unless tariffs stay structurally high or outages repeat.

analogues.name: US residential solar 'grid defection' predicted after net-metering rollbacks
analogues.mechanism: Rising retail tariffs and policy hostility were forecast to drive mass self-supply and utility death spiral.
analogues.lesson: Important negative case: California NEM 3.0 and high rates produced attach-rate growth in storage but an outright *contraction* in US residential solar volumes in 2024–25 on financing costs and installer bankruptcies. High rates cut both ways — they raise tariffs but also kill consumer-financed hardware. At ~5% risk-free, the residential leg is far weaker than the corporate leg.

analogues.name: Dollarisation / private currency substitution in Argentina, Turkey, Venezuela
analogues.mechanism: Loss of faith in a state-provided guarantee (money) leads households to bear real cost to hold a private/foreign substitute, and the behaviour never fully reverses.
analogues.lesson: Trust, once broken in a public guarantee, does not restore on the same timescale it was lost — hysteresis is the rule. Applies directly to whether outage-preparedness search stays structurally elevated after events fade.

analogues.name: Hyperscaler direct nuclear/gas PPAs and BTM campuses (Microsoft–Constellation, Meta gas plants, Amazon–Talen/Generac)
analogues.mechanism: Load growth outruns interconnection; the largest buyers bypass the public grid queue by contracting or building firm generation directly.
analogues.lesson: Already happening and accelerating — this is the leg of the thesis with the shortest path to confirmation. The binding constraint is turbine/transformer/EPC supply and permitting, not demand or willingness to pay.

analogues.name: Private firefighting services for insured high-value homes (California, Colorado)
analogues.mechanism: Insurers and wealthy households buy a parallel private version of an emergency public service as public capacity is overwhelmed.
analogues.lesson: Insurers, not consumers, can be the buyer of resilience. Watch for homeowners' insurers subsidising or mandating backup power/storage — that would be the single fastest distribution channel available.

reference_class.description: Reference class: 'private substitution for a degrading or capacity-constrained public/universal-service guarantee, where the substitute is a durable capital good bought by households and firms.' Members span water (bottled/filtration), security (alarms, guards, gated communities), health (parallel private tiers), connectivity (redundant ISP paths), money (dollarisation) and — most directly — electricity (South Africa, Japan post-Fukushima, Nigeria/India gensets, PURPA cogeneration, Texas Uri, hyperscaler PPAs). The class divides cleanly into two sub-classes with different base rates: (a) ENTERPRISE substitution, where the loss function is quantified, the buyer is sophisticated, purchase is capex-financed and the pattern occurred in ~90% of cases within 3–15 years (UPS/N+1, cogeneration, private guards, hyperscaler PPAs); and (b) HOUSEHOLD substitution, where adoption is event-triggered, consumer-credit-sensitive and slower — pattern occurred in roughly 70% of cases but with 4–25 year mainstreaming times and frequent partial reversion (European gas crisis 2022, post-Uri backlog unwind, US resi solar 2024–25). Typical successful cases required THREE conditions jointly: repeated (not single) failure events, a structural rise in the price of the public option, and a collapse in the installation/financing friction of the private option. Median years-to-mainstream across the occurring cases is ~10; the electricity-specific cases cluster at 3–7 years when failures repeat annually.
reference_class.caveats: Selection bias: the vivid cases (South Africa, Nigeria, Lebanon) come from grids with 100–1,000x the outage frequency of US/EU systems; SAIDI in Germany is ~12 minutes/year and in most of the US ~2–8 hours including major events, so the US/EU baseline may simply never cross the salience threshold outside Texas, California and a few EU member states. The thesis bundles two very differently-based legs — the corporate/BTM leg is near-confirmed and the residential-unit-doubling leg is the genuinely uncertain one; scoring them together inflates apparent confidence. A ~5% risk-free rate is a strong counterweight specific to this cycle: every residential analogue that succeeded did so under cheap consumer financing or heavy subsidy, and the 2024–25 US resi solar contraction is direct evidence that high rates can suppress hardware demand even while fear and tariffs rise. Measurement is fragile: generator unit shipments are partly reported by a single dominant issuer (Generac) whose disclosure changes, EU BESS statistics are collected inconsistently across member states, and Google Trends indices are non-stationary and reflexive to news cycles — the search leg is the weakest and least independent of the three. Base rates also ignore the possibility of the public guarantee being *restored* via grid capex, demand-flexibility software and faster interconnection reform, which would make this a 5-year spike rather than a regime change; and policy could pre-empt private substitution by forcing hyperscalers to fund shared transmission instead of building BTM.

evidence.claim: Amazon awarded Generac an ~$8B generator contract for data-centre backup/bridging power, the single largest behind-the-meter genset order ever disclosed by a hyperscaler (stock +40% on the day).

Electricity availability, not GPU supply, is now the binding constraint on AI buildout — corroborated independently by Oracle filing a force majeure notice on a data-centre project, Meta funding seven gas plants, Mitsui contracting LNG explicitly for data centres, and Talen's data-centre framework progress.

Consumer search interest in 'power grid failure', 'power grid threat' and 'power outage' has been persistently elevated in the attention dataset alongside AI data-centre queries ('ai data center near me', 'ai data center water usage'), indicating households are linking local grid stress to the buildout.

Interconnection queues of 5–7 years in PJM/ERCOT and most EU TSOs mean behind-the-meter generation is bought as a schedule product, not a price product; developers and IPPs are already selling turnkey BTM gas/fuel-cell packages to close that gap.

Nvidia, Google and Anthropic backed Emerald AI specifically to manufacture grid headroom via flexible load — capital is being deployed on the assumption that public grid capacity will not arrive on time.

Policy is turning enabling: Italy reversed a 40-year nuclear ban, EU member states and PJM/ERCOT are drafting data-centre BTM carve-outs, and FERC 2222 aggregation plus state resilience rebates lower the regulatory friction to private firm supply.
Utilities are guiding load growth higher (Duke, Constellation raising 2026), confirming demand is outrunning planned supply — the precondition for scarcity-priced firm power and private substitution.

The reference behaviour has already fully occurred in analogue jurisdictions (South Africa load-shedding → rooftop solar/battery boom; Nigeria/India/Lebanon diesel gensets as default; post-Fukushima Japanese corporate self-generation), showing the mechanism reliably completes once perceived failure probability crosses a salience threshold.

Residential generator and battery demand is historically event-spiky and mean-reverting: Generac's post-Uri 2021 surge fully unwound by 2023, and German/Italian residential BESS installs fell sharply after subsidy and net-metering rollbacks in 2024–25. A 2.0x sustained unit-sales level in 2031 requires a structural break, not a storm.
evidence.source: Generac/EU BESS shipment history (SolarPower Europe, company filings)

evidence.claim: The cost-of-capital regime is hostile to household resilience capex: 30-year mortgage at 7.45% (20-month high), 10-year near 5.15%, Fed pricing hikes not cuts. Financed $10k–$20k standby/battery purchases become discretionary for exactly the middle-income cohort needed to move units from 'innovators' to 'majority'.

Consumer bifurcation caps the addressable base: value-retail leadership, weak housing turnover and a squeezed levered consumer mean the bottom two income quintiles cannot buy reliability at all, so defection is concentrated in a wealthy minority — sufficient for a political story, possibly insufficient for a 2x unit count.

A +15pp shift in large-enterprise load to BTM or ≥5-year firm PPA within six years is an extreme rate of change versus the observed PPA/BTM base rate (roughly 2–4pp per year growth in disclosed corporate firm contracting), and hyperscalers are a small share of total Fortune 500 / STOXX 600 load.

Housing turnover collapse (Lennar miss and delivery cut, one-year-low builder confidence, -4.7% contract signings) removes the new-construction bundling channel, historically the cheapest route to mass installation of standby generators and integrated storage.

Air-permit runtime limits (California BAAQMD, EU IED), noise ordinances, HOA rules and battery siting codes are tightening as BTM density rises; several EU member states are also taxing self-consumption to defend the tariff base.

If AI capex proves to be a financing event rather than a demand event (circular vendor financing — Nvidia into Anthropic, vendor-linked cloud commitments; Burry shorts; Apple's local-inference cost-per-token claim), the incremental enterprise load that drives the enterprise leg of this thesis could arrive materially smaller than currently contracted.

prerequisites_met: Salience shock delivered repeatedly (Uri, EU gas crisis 2022, wildfire PSPS, visible AI data-centre siting fights)
Enterprise economics unambiguous: $M/hour outage cost plus 5–7 year interconnection queues make BTM a schedule purchase
Supply chain exists at scale: aeroderivative turbines, recips, LFP cells, hybrid inverters, fuel cells, smart panels with ATS
Distribution rails built: big-box retail for portables, dealer/solar installer networks for standby+storage, EPC/IPP channel for corporates
Certification and trust rails in place (UL 9540, NFPA, CE) and lender/insurer acceptance improving
Enabling regulation emerging (FERC 2222, state resilience rebates, drafted data-centre BTM carve-outs)
A marquee anchor transaction exists (Amazon–Generac ~$8B) that legitimises the category for boards
prerequisites_missing: Affordability at a 5% risk-free rate — household unit economics still require either a subsidy, a VPP revenue stream, or mortgage-embedded financing that does not exist at scale
Recurring-revenue monetisation (VPP/capacity payments) is not yet default-enrolled at point of sale in most US states and almost nowhere in the EU
New-construction bundling channel is frozen by the housing volume crash
Installer/electrician labour supply is the binding constraint on residential throughput, not demand
A regulatory settlement on who pays the stranded grid cost — absent this, tariff and permit backlash is a live throttle
Standardised, insurable, financeable 'resilience-as-a-service' product for SMBs (the largest untouched segment)
stage.historical_pathway_position: Roughly where US home-security systems sat in the early 1990s or where South African residential solar sat in 2021: the mechanism is proven, the anchor buyers (enterprises, wealthy households) have committed, the product is certified and distributed, but the cost curve and financing wrapper have not yet crossed the threshold for the middle of the distribution. The enterprise leg is at early majority; the consumer leg is at late innovators/early adopters. Historically the ratchet is one-way once installed (sunk capital, fixed fuel connection, property-tied financing), so the level, not the growth rate, is the durable variable.

bull.description: One or two vivid multi-day grid failures in a major US metro or EU member state during 2027–2029 — plausibly attributed in media to data-centre load — converts reliability into a political and status consumption category. Retail tariffs rise 30–50% cumulatively on grid-hardening and transmission capex, widening the spread against self-generated kWh; VPP/capacity enrolment becomes default at point of sale and turns the battery into a cash-flowing asset; plug-in battery kits and smart panels collapse installed cost below $6k. Enterprises complete the shift they have already contracted: BTM gas, fuel cells and nuclear PPAs clear +15pp of large-enterprise load and hyperscalers become de facto IPPs. All three thresholds clear; unit shipments run 2.5–3x 2025. Value accrues violently to firm-MW owners, gas/LNG supply, electrical equipment and the installer channel.

base.description: The enterprise leg clears decisively and the consumer leg clears partially. Corporate BTM/firm-PPA coverage rises meaningfully (roughly +8 to +14pp, short of the formal threshold in aggregate but well above it for the hyperscaler/data-centre subset), and outage-preparedness search stays structurally elevated (index 110–135) because AI siting fights and tariff increases keep the topic salient. Residential/commercial unit shipments grow strongly but at a 1.4–1.8x level rather than 2.0x, throttled by installer labour, 5%+ financing costs and a frozen new-build channel. Thesis is 'directionally confirmed, formally unmet' — reliability is priced as a private good at the enterprise and affluent-household level, while the public guarantee persists for the median ratepayer at a higher tariff. Investable outcome is nearly identical to bull for the equipment/fuel/EPC layer; materially weaker for consumer-facing genset and retail names.

bear.description: AI load growth disappoints relative to contracted plans (financing event, local inference migration, Huawei/China bifurcation), utilities and regulators recapture the load with fast-tracked interconnection, co-location tariffs and explicit data-centre carve-outs that keep large customers on the grid. Residential demand proves storm-spiky and mean-reverts as it did post-Uri and post-2022 EU energy crisis; net-metering rollbacks, self-consumption taxes and air-permit limits bite; the 5% rate regime and the housing volume crash suppress household capex. Search interest normalises within 18 months of the last salient outage. Unit shipments end 2031 at 1.0–1.3x 2025 and the thesis fails on both the primary and secondary legs — with the specific loser being anyone who capitalised the 2026 order book as a run-rate.

supporting: Hyperscaler genset/turbine order announcements beyond the Amazon–Generac deal (GEV, CAT, Cummins, Bloom backlog and delivery-slot pricing)
Aeroderivative turbine and reciprocating engine lead times extending past 2029 — the cleanest scarcity read
Rising share of Generac/Kohler/Briggs revenue from C&I and data-centre channel vs residential storm demand
EU BESS residential install run-rate re-accelerating despite subsidy withdrawal (proof of unsubsidised economics)
Retail electricity tariff increases approved in PJM, ERCOT, California, Germany and Ireland — the spread that funds defection
Corporate 10-K/CSRD disclosure of BTM capacity and ≥5-year firm PPAs; LevelTen/BNEF contracted volume by nuclear and gas
Google Trends 12m MA of the fixed outage basket holding above 120 without a storm catalyst
Home Depot/Lowe's SKU velocity in generators, transfer switches and portable power stations in non-hurricane quarters
VPP enrolment counts and capacity-market revenue per installed residential battery
Insurers offering premium credits for on-site backup (the financialisation signal)
contradictory: Interconnection queue times falling materially in PJM/ERCOT/Germany — removes the schedule motive for BTM
State or EU-level self-consumption taxes, net-metering terminations or standby charges that destroy household payback
Air-permit and runtime-hour restrictions on data-centre gensets spreading beyond California
Generac/Kohler residential order intake mean-reverting within 12 months of the last storm
Hyperscaler capex guidance cuts or further force-majeure/cancellation notices indicating the load never arrives
Local inference migration (Apple cost-per-token claim, edge AI query surge) measurably slowing data-centre power procurement
Utility-offered 'resilience-as-a-service' products re-capturing customers inside the regulated rate base rather than outside it
indicators.next_confirmation_signal: Within two quarters: whether a second hyperscaler signs a multi-billion-dollar behind-the-meter generation or firm-power contract on the Amazon–Generac template, and whether Generac's Q4 2026/Q1 2027 disclosure shows C&I/data-centre backlog growing faster than storm-driven residential. A second anchor deal converts this from a single-buyer anomaly into a category; its absence by mid-2027 is the strongest available falsifier of the enterprise leg.
biggest_variables: Whether a vivid, televised multi-day outage in a major US or EU metro occurs before 2029 — the salience trigger that moves the consumer leg from early adopters to early majority
The path of retail electricity tariffs: grid-hardening and transmission capex recovery is what mechanically funds private defection
Cost of capital — a 5% risk-free rate is the single largest suppressant of household resilience capex; a rate regime change is the biggest swing factor on the unit-sales threshold
Whether regulators socialise or allocate data-centre grid costs; allocation keeps hyperscalers on the grid, socialisation triggers ratepayer backlash and accelerates defection
Real AI load delivery versus contracted load — the difference between a demand event and a financing event
Electrician/installer labour supply in the US and EU, which caps residential throughput regardless of demand
Gas and LPG fuel price stability — the operating-cost leg of the household payback calculation

value_pools.layer: Firm dispatchable generation assets (existing nuclear, CCGT, peakers)
value_pools.emerging_need: Contracted, schedulable MW with a delivery date inside 36 months
value_pools.opportunity: Repricing of every merchant MW from a commodity to a long-dated contracted annuity; nuclear PPAs signed at multiples of prior power-curve assumptions

value_pools.layer: Power generation and electrical equipment OEMs
value_pools.emerging_need: Turbines, gensets, switchgear, transformers, transfer switches, busway and thermal management delivered on a schedule, not a price
value_pools.opportunity: Delivery slots become the product; multi-year backlogs with price escalators and customer prepayments; margin expansion from allocation rather than volume

value_pools.emerging_need: Physically building substations, BTM plants, interconnections and residential installs faster than the utility queue
value_pools.opportunity: Labour scarcity converts EPC and mechanical contracting into a pricing-power business; the electrician is the bottleneck of the entire thesis

value_pools.emerging_need: Firm molecule delivery to BTM plants and residential propane/nat-gas standby units
value_pools.opportunity: Long-dated firm gas contracts and lateral pipelines to data-centre campuses; LNG-to-power packages sold as reliability rather than commodity

value_pools.emerging_need: Households buying portable power stations, standby units, transfer switches and install services
value_pools.opportunity: High-ticket, high-attach, service-linked category growth in exactly the retailers the market has marked for the housing recession; also fits the repair-and-stay-put behavioural shift
LFP + hybrid inverter + smart panel bundles; the asset that is both insurance and an income stream once aggregation is default-enrolled

value_pools.emerging_need: Manufacturing headroom on a constrained grid; flexible-load contracts; VPP dispatch across millions of edge assets
value_pools.opportunity: A thin, high-multiple software layer on a physical constraint — Emerald-AI-type products, utility DERMS, industrial load flexing

value_pools.emerging_need: Copper, steel, aluminium and industrial gases for duplicated generation and distribution infrastructure
value_pools.opportunity: Private redundancy means the same load is wired twice; structurally raises metal intensity per delivered kWh

value_pools.layer: Regulated utilities with residential-heavy rate base
value_pools.emerging_need: Recovering grid-hardening capex from a shrinking, poorer remaining customer base
value_pools.opportunity: Rate-base growth is real but political risk rises; the ones that win sell resilience-as-a-service inside the rate base rather than fighting defection

value_pools.emerging_need: Power procurement becomes the primary underwriting risk, ahead of land, capital or tenant credit

second_order_thesis: The consensus trade is 'buy the generator company'. That is the first-order, and it is the leg most likely to mean-revert. The second-order insight is that what is actually being repriced is not electrons but *time-to-power* — a firm MW with a 2029 delivery date is now a different, scarcer asset than a MW with a 2034 date, and every layer that shortens the delivery date (turbine slots, switchgear, electricians, EPC capacity, permitted brownfield sites, existing nuclear) captures the rent, while every layer that merely supplies energy does not. This is why the equipment and trades layer, not the utility or the fuel, is where pricing power migrates. The deeper second-order effect is fiscal and political: each defector removes a high-margin customer from the pool funding universal-service reliability, raising tariffs for those who remain, which accelerates the next defection — a classic adverse-selection death spiral identical to the mechanism that hollowed out public schooling, municipal water (bottled water), and policing (private security). That spiral does not resolve in the market; it resolves in regulation. Expect the binding 2028–2031 variable to be a political settlement over who pays stranded grid cost — standby charges, exit fees, self-consumption taxes, data-centre cost-allocation dockets — which makes regulated utilities a political-risk asset rather than a bond proxy, and makes the residential leg of the thesis structurally throttled at exactly the moment the economics finally work. Third order: because the installed base ratchets (sunk capital, fixed fuel connection, property-tied financing), the level is permanent even if the flow disappoints, which means the durable investment is in the *service and fuel annuity* on an installed base — maintenance, propane/gas delivery, VPP aggregation, firmware and warranty — not in the unit-shipment cycle the market currently trades. Finally, reliability becoming a purchased good is a regressive event: it creates a two-tier electricity system in which the wealthy and the corporate buy availability and the median ratepayer buys a more expensive, less reliable grid. That is the single most under-priced input to 2029–2031 utility regulation, retail energy politics, and the value-retail/consumer-bifurcation theme.
losers: Regulated vertically-integrated utilities with residential-heavy, low-growth rate bases facing defection by their highest-margin customers plus rising political risk on cost allocation (DUK, SO, AEP, and NEE's regulated arm)
Net-lease and duration-proxy REITs already pressured by a 5%+ long bond and now facing higher operating energy costs and resilience capex (O, SPG)
Data-centre REITs and colocation operators without secured firm power or BTM capacity, whose land banks cannot be energised on schedule (EQIX, DLR)

Second-tier neoclouds and equity-funded compute landlords — the AI drawdown arrives as a financing event and they cannot outbid hyperscalers for firm MW (ORCL's data-centre development arm is the listed proxy)
Homebuilders, doubly hit: frozen turnover removes the bundling channel while rising grid-connection and resilience costs add to cost per unit (LEN, DHI, PHM, TOL)

Low-income and renter households — structurally excluded from private reliability while bearing the tariff increases funding grid hardening; bearish for levered-consumer credit exposure (AXP, SOFI) and supportive of value retail
Diesel-dependent backup vendors facing tightening air-permit runtime limits in California and under the EU IED
Pure commodity power merchants with no firm contracting or nuclear/gas optionality — the value moves to contracted, not merchant, MW
Standalone battery and solar hardware vendors without VPP monetisation or installer networks — hardware becomes abundant and commoditised while installation and dispatch stay scarce

probability.note: Posterior log-odds = prior log-odds (reference-class base rate) + sum of quality x independence weighted log likelihood ratios. Research-informed estimate until enough theses resolve for Brier calibration.

source_bullets.text: Energy self-reliance: households and enterprises increasingly want to own their generation and resilience \u2014 'power grid failure/threat/outage' queries alongside Amazon buying generators. Reliability becomes a purchased good, not a public utility assumption.

Energy is becoming a status and security good, not a commodity line item: district heating investment, LNG contracting for data centers, pipeline races and grid-failure searches all reflect a population and a corporate sector paying up for guaranteed electrons.
